statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 12% in the low band, Stress 72% high, Confidence 87% high, with CME equity futures halted for the weekend across every published hour.
recommendation: Tail is published below the 20% watch threshold for all 24 hours because no hour in the window contains a tradable session, so the mapped policy state is EA_ON throughout and no danger window is published. Friday's record cash close arrived 209.60 points under the session's own intraday high and NQ settled 233.25 below its high with VIX a cent off its low, which is retracement rather than the persistent no-retracement path Tail is built to detect. Stress stays in the high band because the long-end yield reversal, the elevated energy complex, the G7 reserve release timetable and the Middle East supply threat are unresolved rather than resolved. The first scheduled high-impact checkpoint, ISM Services on 5 October at 14:00Z, sits outside this window, as does the 22:00Z Sunday futures reopen.
headline: Cash NDX takes a record close at 30,807.93 yet finishes 209.60 under its own session high, NQ settles 31,049.00 and VIX decays 6.59% to 15.31, leaving Tail at 12% with futures halted for the weekend
body:
Cash NDX closed 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00%, from a 30,869.14 open and a 30,501.56 previous close, inside a 30,737.07-31,017.53 session range. That is a record close, and it is also 209.60 points, 0.68%, below the session's own 31,017.53 intraday high, which now stands as the 52-week high. The index therefore set a closing record while retracing from its intraday extreme rather than finishing on it. NQ December futures settled 31,049.00, up 288.50 or 0.94%, on a final 20:59:58Z print, inside a 30,760.25-31,282.25 range from a 30,771.25 open on 573.48k contracts, 233.25 below their own session high. Both legs of the market ended the week pulling back from their highs, which is the structure that argues against a pathological no-retracement path.

Volatility confirmed it. VIX closed 15.31, down 1.08 or 6.59%, from a 16.15 open and a 16.39 previous close, inside a 15.30-16.24 range, settling a single cent above its session low. The macro trigger was the September Employment Situation at 12:30Z: nonfarm payrolls rose 29,000 against a consensus near 90,000, the unemployment rate ticked up to 4.2% from 4.1%, and average hourly earnings rose just 0.1% on the month against 0.3% expected, with August revised to 133,000. Markets read it as removing a near-term tightening risk, and the implied probability of an October rate hike fell to roughly 15-16%.

The cross-asset picture is not uniformly calm, which is why Stress stays high at 72% while Tail falls to 12%. The front end and the long end both reversed higher after an initial post-payroll fall: the 2-year closed about 4.8414%, up 5.44 basis points, and the 10-year about 5.2939%, up 5.99 basis points, ending above Thursday's levels even as equities set a record close. The H.15 release dated 2 October, carrying 1 October data, shows 2-year 4.78%, 10-year 5.24% and 30-year 5.61%. Energy remains a live shock: WTI eased 1.73% to about $91.26 after touching a one-month low of $88.06 intraday, and Brent held about $102.70, up 0.38%, but WTI is still roughly 49.9% above a year ago and Brent about 59.2%. The G7, coordinating with the IEA, agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel over four months, with a substantial diesel volume front-loaded into the first 20 days. Behind that sit reported additional U.S. naval deployments to the Middle East and a reported Houthi-Saudi campaign threatening Saudi export capacity, both treated here as secondary context rather than primary-verified evidence.

The decisive fact for the published forecast is structural: CME equity futures halted at 21:00Z on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday. All 24 published hours run inside that halt, Saturday carries no scheduled U.S. macro release, and the reopen falls about 25 hours beyond the end of this window. Tail measures the risk that mean reversion fails against a persistent one-way path, and a closed market provides no path at all, so Tail eases from 12% to a 9% floor across the deep Saturday hours and drifts back only to 11% by the close of the window. That late drift is explicitly conditional and gap-shaped; no halted hour can establish the shallow pullbacks, repeated extension or session-extreme holding that Tail is built to detect. The shared Finviz context was not used: the file carries a 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z collection time, roughly 71 hours old, with a partial collection status and both its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it was treated as unhealthy and the assessment rests entirely on independent verified research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published Claude hours are available, covering the 22:00Z hour on 1 October through the 21:00Z hour on 2 October. Tail ran from 14% to 27% across the window. It opened at 20% and held that watch floor for nine consecutive hours through the Asian session, then stepped to 21% at 07:00Z, 23% at 08:00Z and 22% at 09:00Z on the European-morning advance, before returning to 20% at 10:00Z and 11:00Z. The 12:30Z payroll release drove the only escalation: Tail reached 24% at 12:00Z, crossed into the elevated band at 25% for the 13:00Z hour and peaked at 27% at 14:00Z, the two hours spanning the release and the 13:30Z cash open, which published orange and BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. It then de-escalated as fast as it rose, back to 22% by 15:00Z, holding 22-23% through the cash session, easing to 21% at 20:00Z and reaching the window's 14% low at 21:00Z as the Friday close resolved benignly and futures halted. Stress stayed in the high band throughout, between 74% and 79%, and Confidence held 86-89%. Dominant mode was mixed for 19 hours, with trend-up published for the 08:00Z and 09:00Z European advance and for the 12:00Z through 14:00Z payroll reaction. The window is a complete record of a large labor-market surprise that briefly lifted Tail into the block band and then resolved without producing a persistent one-way path.
outlookSummary: The forecast opens at 12% for the current 22:00Z hour, two points below the preceding published hour, because the halt has now been in force for over an hour with no venue able to extend Friday's move. The observed close supports the low band: cash NDX took a record close yet finished 209.60 below its own intraday high, NQ settled 233.25 under its session high, and VIX ended a cent off its low. The structural fact governing all 24 hours is that CME equity futures halted at 21:00Z and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, roughly 25 hours after this window ends. No published hour contains a tradable session and Saturday carries no scheduled U.S. macro release, so Tail is published in the low band throughout: it eases through the Friday evening hours, settles at a 9% floor across the deep Saturday stretch from 04:00Z to 11:00Z, then drifts back to 11% by 21:00Z as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates. That drift is explicitly conditional and gap-shaped. Stress is published between 68% and 72%, easing as Friday's volatility decay carries forward and firming late as the G7 release timetable and reported Middle East supply risk stay unpriced. Confidence decays from 87% to a 77% floor, remaining in the high band because coverage of index, futures, volatility, yields, energy and the seven-day calendar is complete and verified; what ages across the halt is the price path, not the research. Mode is published as mixed for the three hours still shaped by Friday's cross-asset conflict and normal for the 21 hours in which no market structure exists to classify. No danger window is published and the mapped policy state is EA_ON for all 24 hours. The first scheduled high-impact checkpoints, ISM Services on 5 October and the FOMC minutes on 7 October, sit beyond the window.
